data.body: files.edit line-ending rule (task 214). `edit_file` matches line endings tolerantly: an exact byte match first, then a unique match with CRLF/lone CR normalised to LF, and a normalised match that occurs twice is still refused as ambiguous. Indentation is not normalised because it is semantic. The written file keeps its own convention - untouched bytes are byte-identical and inserted lines adopt the ending of the line they join - and the result reports `lineEnding` and `lineEndingsReconciled`. `write_file` is unchanged and still writes exactly the content it is given. The old "byte for byte ... after normalising CRLF" miss message is gone, so it no longer indicates a code path; a miss now means the text really is absent or differs in something other than line endings. Module: desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop/line_endings.rs.
